subject: Control gap heatmap and escalation plan for ISO/FedRAMP intake
messages:
From: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@atlasfintech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.example>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@auditfirm.io>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Intake: control mapping and timing for procurement

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. As part of AtlasFintech's vendor assessment we need two things in the next 10 business days: a control-level mapping that shows which Redwood controls map to ISO 27001 clauses and FedRAMP baselines, and a simple heatmap that highlights gaps where we will need compensating controls or attestation language.

Deliverables we want:
- Control mapping CSV (control id -> ISO clause -> FedRAMP control id)
- Heatmap (red/amber/green) and short rationale for each red/amber item
- Owner for each piece of evidence and estimated delivery date

Also flag any controls that rely on third-party or shared services (cloud provider, monitoring vendor). Our procurement legal will use this to set acquisition timelines.

Can you confirm you have an owner and a delivery date by end of this week? We have an initial legal review scheduled 2026-11-15.

Appreciate it —
Sandra
Director, Vendor Risk
AtlasFintech

---
[Attachment: vendor_request_summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.example>
To: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@atlasfintech.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.example>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intake: control mapping and timing for procurement

Sandra —

Thanks, we can do this. High-level plan below and I've attached an initial heatmap draft and evidence manifest for your review.

Planned deliverables & owners:
- Control mapping CSV (Kimberly / Rishi) — initial draft 2026-11-05, final 2026-11-09
- Heatmap v1 (Markus) — draft attached (redwood_control_heatmap_v1.xlsx), commentary in the "notes" tab
- Evidence manifest (Grace) — attached (evidence_manifest_kp_v2.pdf), includes sample doc locations and responsible names

Scope notes: we map to ISO 27001:2013 controls and to FedRAMP Low/Moderate where applicable. Anything that falls under our cloud provider (KMS, network isolation) is noted as "shared/3p". We will flag those with recommended compensating language.

Open asks (please confirm):
1) For controls that require deployment-level artifacts (network diagrams, runbooks), do you require anonymized artifacts or full internal diagrams?
2) Do you need auditor-facing narratives (control assertions) or is the mapping + heatmap sufficient for procurement?

Next steps: I will circulate the CSV draft on 11/05. If you want a 30-min walkthrough of the heatmap when the draft is ready, we can schedule next week.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_control_heatmap_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.example>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.example>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.example>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.example>, Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@atlasfintech.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T14:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intake: control mapping and timing for procurement

Looping in auditor availability and pre-audit expectations. Tom — any concerns about the proposed timeline (final deliverable by 11/09, legal review 11/15)?

From our side:
- We can produce an honest heatmap, but expect 8-12 items flagged as amber/red that will require either evidence collection or compensating language.
- We propose a 2-hour dry-run with an auditor to validate narratives and evidence sampling before legal gets the packet. Prefer week of 11/08.

Tom — do you have capacity to do a dry-run on 11/09 or 11/10? If not, earliest available dates? Also, if the auditor can indicate which artifacts they would want to actually validate (logs, runbooks, change records) that will help us prioritize.

-Markus
Director, Trust Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Wu <tom.wu@auditfirm.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.example>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intake: control mapping and timing for procurement

Markus/Kimberly —

We can do a 90–120 minute dry-run on 2026-11-09 at 09:00 PT. During the session we'll: walk control narratives, request 2–3 sample artifacts per red control, and give a gap list with suggested remediation language. Please make sure evidence owners are on the call.

Preliminary note: auditors frequently ask for "time-bounded" evidence — e.g., log extracts for a 30-day window rather than entire retention buckets. If you can prepare extracts and a short extraction playbook it speeds validation.

I'll circulate a short pre-brief doc and checklist.

-Tom
Senior Manager, Assurance
AuditFirm LLP

[Attachment: auditor_prebrief_notes.docx (docx)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.example>

Quick update —
- Control CSV draft uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-heatmap (see file mapping_ctrls_20261105.csv)

Kimberly — do you want me to open a JIRA ticket for the product team or route through Markus for escalation?

Thanks,
Grace
